hidden_case.description: Tested whether the SAME real file, reachable through two syntactically different but filesystem-equivalent path strings (one containing a '..' backreference), is falsely reported as a 'renamed-clone' of itself. The tool's dedup in _files() is based on syntactic Path-object equality, not realpath/inode identity.

hidden_case.analysis: A real, single file is reported as a 'renamed-clone' of itself when reached via overlapping/aliased input roots. This is plausible in real PO-03 usage where a caller might scan overlapping directories or symlinked paths. The detector lacks realpath-based deduplication before pairwise comparison. (A simpler alias test using pathlib's own '.' collapsing did NOT reproduce the bug, since PurePath silently drops single '.' segments; the '..'-based alias was required to demonstrate it.)

disposition_reason: The required deliverable (a content-similarity detector flagging near-duplicate/renamed-clone pairs with hashes) is implemented correctly and demonstrated on both an exact clone and a near-duplicate, with a true negative on unrelated content. All 8 acceptance criteria are met and tests are non-vacuous. The hidden-case self-clone false positive under overlapping/aliased roots is a real defect worth fixing (via os.path.realpath-based dedup) but is a robustness gap rather than a violation of the frozen acceptance wording.
